It's offshore, so the shape is there, it's just a lot of wind and a 4.6ft @ 5s NNW chop riding through the line-up. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold FAIR through the morning; Dee Why and Manly sit POOR-FAIR. Energy collapses fast after 11am — 420 kJ at noon, 331 by 3pm — so the swell and the calm never overlap today. Tuesday resets: 2–3ft and 168 kJ at dawn with a light W offshore easing to 11–13 km/h by midday (the cleanest window of the next 48h), then a new pulse arrives in the afternoon — 426 kJ at 3pm, 614 kJ and 4.7–5.6ft by 5pm. Saturday is the small, clean one: 2–3ft, 41–90 kJ, WSW–SW offshore 8 km/h all morning before a SSE onshore from mid-afternoon. Sunday is beyond the model's 6-day range and is flagged estimated. — Surf Guru agent

days.label: Today
days.note: Plenty of swell, too much wind. 915 kJ and a 7.2ft @ 9s ENE at 57° — that's the angle you want — but NW 30+ km/h gusting 51–76 is on it from before dawn and only builds. Long Reef and Curl Curl are the only two holding FAIR; go early or don't go. Energy more than halves after 11am, so there is no clean-and-big window today.

swells.label: Primary ENE groundswell — the direction Dee Why actually uses
5s NNW chop generated by the gale — this is what's messing up the faces

dee-why.window: 6:00–8:30am and that's it. Wind is lightest at dawn (27–30 km/h gusting 46–51) and the 6:12am high (1.2m) gives the Point some water. By 10am it's 32 gusting 64 and the 11:40am low (0.4m) has the banks sucking dry. 1139 kJ at 6am → 915 at 9am → 420 by noon.
alerts: NW gale gusting 51 at dawn, 76 by midday, 81 by 3pm — offshore but genuinely strong
4.6ft of 5s NNW wind chop through the line-up on top of the groundswell

tip.label: Point over beachie, but only at dawn
tip.text: 57° ENE at 9s is the angle that switches the Point on — frontside rights for you, and at 4–6ft it will have a real wall. The problem is the 5s NNW chop and 30+ km/h of it. Sit wider than usual, take the first of the set before the chop stands it up, and be honest about the paddle-out: this is a strong-arm day, not a cruise.

swells.label: Primary ENE — Long Reef takes the most of it, as always

long-reef.window: 6:00–10:00am. Pick of the four again and by a bigger margin than usual: 6.1–7.4ft at 9am off the same 915 kJ that only gives Dee Why 4–6ft. Holds FAIR right through the morning while Dee Why and Manly sit poor-fair.
alerts: Solid — head to 2ft overhead with a gale on it. Sets will hold up and the NW will hold you at the top of the drop

tip.label: Biggest of the four — respect it
tip.text: A foot and a half more than Dee Why off identical energy. You're backside on the lefts off the point, and with 30+ km/h of NW holding the lip you'll get held up on the drop — commit early and low, don't stall for the barrel that the wind is going to blow open anyway.

curl-curl.window: 6:00–9:30am. Rates FAIR alongside Long Reef and it's the closer drive. North Curl Curl corner will be the sheltered option if the NW gets on top of you at the open beach.
alerts: Rips will be serious at 5–7ft with the 11:40am low draining the banks

tip.label: Use the north corner
tip.text: At 5–7ft with a NW gale the open bank is a washing machine. The north corner sits in the lee of the headland and gives you a defined take-off — frontside rights off the rocks, which is your good side.

swells.label: Primary ENE — Manly gets a decent share of this angle

manly.window: 6:00–8:30am. Same poor-fair rating as Dee Why but a foot bigger. Really only worth it if you want the Queenscliff bommie end away from the crowd.
alerts: Closeouts likely on the open North Steyne banks at this size with 5s chop through it

tip.label: Queenscliff end or skip it
tip.text: North Steyne will be a shorebreak lottery at 5–6ft. If you're here, walk to the Queenscliff end where the bank has more shape — otherwise Long Reef is worth the extra 15 minutes today.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The clean day, but small early. 2–3ft and 168 kJ at dawn with W offshore dropping to 11–13 km/h by midday — that's the lightest wind of the next 48 hours. Then it rebuilds through the afternoon: 426 kJ at 3pm and 4.7–5.6ft with 614 kJ by 5pm. If you can get out between 2pm and last light you get size AND clean water.

dee-why.window: Either 11am–1pm for the cleanest (W 11–13 km/h, gusts only 18–20) or 3pm–5:30pm to catch the new pulse arriving — 426 kJ at 3pm building to 614 by 5pm. Sunset 5:22pm, last light 5:48pm.

long-reef.window: Biggest again on the same energy. Morning is clean but modest; the afternoon build is where it gets interesting — be there by 3pm.

curl-curl.window: Light W offshore all day, FAIR from dawn. Best banks of the four for a small clean day — 11am–1pm.

manly.window: Smallest of the four. Only worth it midday if you're already in town — otherwise wait for the 3pm build.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the small, clean, mid-morning one you like the look of — 2–3ft, WSW–SW offshore at 8 km/h from dawn to noon, tide low 0.2m at 3:52am, high 1.4m at 9:57am, so mid-tide push through your 10am–12pm window. Energy is light (41 kJ at 9am, 76 by noon) so it's a fun-board day, not a performance day. The SSE onshore fills in from 3pm. Sunday sits beyond Surfline's 6-day model range this refresh — flagged estimated, will firm up in the next two runs.

dee-why.window: Sat 8am–12pm. WSW 8 km/h offshore, 9:57am high (1.4m) filling in under your usual 10am–12pm slot. Slow, small and clean. Sunday: estimated, not yet in model range.
